chapter.title: Morphological dictionary readers
chapter.para: Stored forms and query tokens use StringUtil.toLowerCase code-point conversion. This maps dotted capital I to i and capital sigma to small sigma without contextual casing. Input-conversion replacements are lower-cased again before lookup; tags and lemmas keep their original case.

section.title: Dictionary lemmatization from PoliMorf tables
section.para: Distinct lemmas for a form and tag retain their first-seen order. A # is part of a lemma, not a separator: an entry csharp C# NNP returns C#, not C. Empty lemma and tag fields are retained; columns after the tag are ignored. Malformed entries and invalid character data cause IOException.

section.title: Reading morfologik dictionaries
section.para: MorfologikDictionaryReader loads FSA5 and CFSA2 .dict files into a DictionaryLemmatizer, without a third-party dependency. Supply a dictionary and .info metadata file, or specify the separator, character encoding and base-form encoder explicitly. Dictionary data is not bundled with OpenNLP.

Loading expands every entry into an in-memory lookup map. Subsequent lookups use that map, not the compressed automaton. Allow heap for decoded forms, tags and lemmas, plus temporary collections during loading. Compressed file size alone does not indicate the heap required.

The metadata file is UTF-8, regardless of the dictionary's encoding. It must declare fsa.dict.separator, fsa.dict.encoding and fsa.dict.encoder. The separator character must encode as a single byte in the dictionary's charset. For example, € is byte 0x80 in Windows-1252 but cannot be a UTF-8 dictionary separator. Invalid separator definitions cause IllegalArgumentException. Surrounding spaces in encoder names are ignored.

Optional fsa.dict.input-conversion metadata supplies ordered string substitutions for query tokens. Each comma-separated entry uses a single space between the input and replacement strings. For example: fsa.dict.input-conversion=\uFB03 ffi, \u2019 ' This expands the U+FB03 ligature to ffi and converts a typographic apostrophe to an ASCII apostrophe, allowing can’t to match can't.

Query tokens are lower-cased before substitution. Rules apply in order to non-overlapping matches; text inserted by a rule is considered only by later rules. Lookup remains case-insensitive after substitution. Tags, stored forms and lemmas are not substituted. Invalid pairs and duplicate input strings cause IllegalArgumentException before the dictionary is read. Spelling options and output-display conversions do not change lemmatizer results.

Decoded tags and lemmas retain characters such as #, tabs and line breaks. Forms are lower-cased to match lookup. Empty fields are retained. Invalid character data in a decoded field, or invalid UTF-8 metadata, causes IOException.

Reachable nodes and arcs are checked on load. Truncated data, invalid addresses, unsupported format flags and cycles cause IOException. Traversal uses a per-call stack without recursive calls. Paths exceeding 8192 bytes and nodes with shared outgoing arcs are supported.

The supported encoders are NONE, SUFFIX, PREFIX and INFIX. Removal counts use bytes, not characters. Encoded control values wrap modulo 256; a removal count of 255 replaces the complete surface form. Control bytes equal to the separator are part of the encoded base, not field boundaries. Incomplete controls and overlapping or out-of-range removals cause IOException on load.
Use PoliMorfDictionaryReader to load a tab-separated PoliMorf table into a DictionaryLemmatizer.
